[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call then we'll get into security and deployment preferences.
[00:08] Lena (Kestral): Hey, Lena here. Thanks. We have Tom and Priya and Evan as well.
[00:12] Tom (CTO): Hey all.
[00:14] Priya (Infra): Hi.
[00:16] Maya: Great. So goal today is to understand Kestral's compliance bar and decide whether Hosted, Dedicated, or Private makes sense. Derrick will walk the technical bits.
[00:25] Derrick (Redwood SE): Cool, I'll jump in. First question for you, Lena — what does your audit scope look like today? SOC 2 only, or ISO too?
[00:32] Lena: We're SOC2 Type II, currently. We're starting ISO 27001 prep — not certified yet, but target Q2 next year. Important for us: ephemeral keys are okay, but for production we need customer-managed keys for certain workloads (BYOK). Also, our enterprise contracts want proof of separation of customer data and immutability of logs.
[00:48] Maya: Good, that's common. For BYOK we support KMS integrations in Dedicated and Private; hosted has an option for external KMS via a bring-your-key flow but there are limitations. I'll follow up with exact doc.
[00:58] Priya: Wait on hosted BYOK — does that mean keys live in our cloud account or Redwood's?
[01:03] Owen (Redwood): In Hosted today keys are managed by Redwood's KMS by default; we offer a customer-managed envelope key option for certain plans, but full BYOK with HSM in your VPC is only available in Dedicated/Private. There's a nuance with cross-account encrypt wrappers — we'll draw it out.
[01:20] Tom: Could you say more about the network boundary for Dedicated vs Private? We're concerned about egress and cross-tenant leaks.
[01:27] Derrick: Yeah. Dedicated gives you isolated GPU pools and tenancy within Redwood's cloud project — logical isolation plus tenant-level network controls. Private gives you the control plane in your VPC (or on-prem) so compute and keys can be fully in your account. Hosted is multitenant and redwood-managed.
[01:41] Speaker 3 (autotagged): mhm, and we have, like, fallback policies if capacity is constrained, right?
[01:46] Maya: Right — we can route to a lower-cost variant, but for customers with strict controls that's disabled.
[01:51] Evan (Legal): On data retention, we have several regulated contracts that require up to seven years of logs. Does Redwood support long-term immutable audit storage?
[02:00] Derrick: We store audit logs in append-only storage and can export to your S3 or your log retention system. For 7+ years, Private or Dedicated with export hookup is easiest; Hosted can export but retention policies depend on plan.
[02:15] Lena: Do you provide cryptographic integrity (e.g., signed logs) for long-term storage? We need evidence in audits that logs haven't been tampered with.
[02:22] Derrick: We can sign log batches with a service-level signing key; for the highest assurance customers we recommend local signing via your HSM in Private. We'll flag that in the architecture doc.
[02:33] Tom: SSO — we run Okta, SAML 2.0, SCIM for provisioning. How mature is your SSO/RBAC integration?
[02:40] Maya: We support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning across Hosted/Dedicated/Private. For RBAC, we have role templates but customers can map Okta groups to Redwood roles. In Private you can also enforce additional constraints with your own identity provider hooks.
[02:54] Priya: Any limitation on SCIM attribute mapping? We need custom attributes for data access policies.
[02:59] Owen: SCIM is flexible; some custom attributes need mapping via a small transformation step in the config. We'll include a sample mapping.
[03:12] Lena: On encryption at rest and in transit — TLS is fine — but we need to know key rotations, key access audits, and whether key material ever leaves our KMS.
[03:22] Derrick: Keys never leave HSM in a proper BYOK setup. For Redwood-managed keys we rotate regularly and maintain key access logs. We surface key access events in audit logs.
[03:31] Priya: For Hosted, if we use the envelope key option, where do the wrapping keys live?
[03:36] Maya: They would live in Redwood's KMS unless you choose a partner-managed flow. We'll send the exact diagrams.
[03:42] Tom: What about model artifacts and KV cache — are those stored encrypted separately per-customer?
[03:48] Derrick: Model weights are read-only and shared; customer KV caches and any persisted user content are stored per-customer and encrypted. For Dedicated/Private you can opt to persist caches in your own storage.
[03:58] Speaker 2 (auto): There's also the question of inference logs and telemetry retention and how they map to billing data.
[04:05] Maya: Good point — customers often want billing deltas without exposing payloads. We have redaction options and token-level cost logs separated from full transcripts.
[04:15] Lena: Ok. Another hard requirement: we need tamper-evident chain of custody for high-risk case transcripts (legal/regulatory). Can Redwood provide notarization or a digest we can store?
[04:27] Owen: We can provide signed digests for transcripts and store those in an append-only ledger or push to your archive. In Private you can entirely control ledger signing.
[04:38] Evan: Vendor security questionnaire — we'll need answers on incident response, data deletion, subcontractors. What's the typical turnaround?
[04:45] Maya: We usually return an initial completed questionnaire within 5 business days for standard items; deeper legal contracts take longer. We'll push the security pack now.
[04:53] Tom: SLA concerns — we need 99.95% and predictable p99 latency during business hours. Which deployment meets that best?
[05:00] Derrick: Dedicated gives you the strongest latency predictability; Private can match it but depends on your infra choices. Hosted has SLOs but shared noisy neighbors can affect p99 unless you pick a higher tier.
[05:12] Priya: If we do Dedicated, who manages upgrades and kernel/microcode for the GPUs?
[05:17] Owen: Redwood manages the serving runtime upgrades in Dedicated. If you pick Private on-prem, your ops team manages hardware and we provide the control plane or an operator package.
[05:29] Lena: About audit logs retention — you mentioned export to S3. For immutability we want write-once-read-many (WORM) buckets and MFA delete. Does Redwood support configuring exports directly into an S3 WORM bucket?
[05:41] Derrick: Yes, we can deliver signed exports directly into your S3 with WORM/MFA-delete set on the destination. We'll note required IAM permissions in the doc.
[05:52] Maya: Quick pause — anything we haven't asked that is a blocker for you?
[05:57] Tom: Cost — private looks expensive. We want a ballpark of baseline monthly runrates for 2k concurrent sessions, and how much the BYOK/HSM add.
[06:06] Maya: We'll provide a sizing + cost spreadsheet. As a rule-of-thumb: Dedicated is ~X–Y% above Hosted for predictable throughput; Private includes infra costs. We'll put numbers in the follow-up.
[06:18] Lena: Last — incident notification and forensics. We'd like a 1-hour P1 notification window and a post-incident forensics packet with signed evidence.
[06:27] Owen: We can commit to an escalation path; legal SLA needs to be defined in the contract for guaranteed timelines. For forensics, Private gives the most control but Dedicated can provide full forensics artifacts upon request.
[06:41] Speaker 4 (auto): there was a small question about data residency — EMEA customers require EU-only processing.
[06:47] Priya: Yes, we need EU-only processing for some lines of business. Can Redwood pin regions?
[06:52] Derrick: We pin regions in Dedicated and Private; Hosted has regional endpoints and we can guarantee residency on certain plans. We'll include table of available regions and data residency guarantees.
[07:05] Lena: Thanks. Maybe we can recap next steps.
[07:08] Maya: Sure — recap: Redwood will share SOC2 Type II report, ISO artifacts, PT summary, and a VPC/KMS architecture sketch comparing Hosted/Dedicated/Private. SE to include notes on signed logs and WORM exports. We'll schedule the technical deep dive for the week of Dec 20. Action items in the notes.
[07:25] Evan: I'll coordinate legal questions and send the vendor questionnaire by end of week.
[07:29] Tom: Sounds good.
[07:31] Maya: Great, thanks everyone, we'll follow up.
